question: Why do solar and lunar eclipses NOT occur every single New Moon and Full Moon day?
options: The Moon's orbital plane around Earth is tilted at an angle of ~5 degrees relative to Earth's orbital plane around the S
explanation: The Moon's orbital plane around Earth is tilted at an angle of ~5 degrees relative to Earth's orbital plane around the Sun. Most New and Full Moons pass slightly above or below the Sun-Earth line, avoiding eclipse alignment.

Why do we always see the same side/face of the Moon from Earth?
options: The Moon's rotation period on its own axis exactly equals its orbital revolution period around Earth (~27.3 days), a phe
explanation: The Moon's rotation period on its own axis exactly equals its orbital revolution period around Earth (~27.3 days), a phenomenon known as tidal locking or synchronous rotation.

question: Explain how Earth's anti-clockwise rotation on its axis creates the apparent east-to-west movement of the Sun and stars.

explanation: Just as a passenger on a clockwise merry-go-round sees surrounding trees spinning anti-clockwise, an observer on Earth rotating from West to East sees celestial bodies (Sun, stars) moving in the opposite direction from East to West.

question: Explain how Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt and revolution around the Sun cause summer and winter seasons in Northern and Southern hemispheres.

explanation: 1. Earth's axis is tilted at 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital plane. 2. When the Northern Hemisphere tilts toward the Sun (June Solstice), it receives direct solar rays for longer hours, causing Summer in the North and Winter in the South. 3. Six months later (December Solstice), Northern Hemisphere tilts away from Sun receiving indirect slanted rays, causing Winter in the North and Summer in the South.
